name: Titanic
label: Unheard of Hope
lede: Mabe Fratti, a Guatemalan cellist, and Héctor Tosta, a Mexico City guitarist-producer, make records the way other people renovate a house, room by room: pop in one, black metal in the next.

eras.title: A cellist leaves the church
eras.text: Mabe Fratti grows up in Guatemala in a Pentecostal household where the only approved music is Christian and classical. When she walks out of the church, the cello is the one thing that comes with her.

years.h: Fratti arrives in Mexico City on a Goethe Institute residency
years.p: [[Mabe Fratti|ddefada4-c07e-43d3-9837-318805f37776]], born in Guatemala in 1992 and trained on cello, comes for the residency and stays for the city's improvising scene.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Fratti grew up in a Pentecostal household, studied classical cello, and widened her listening through file-sharing, a György Ligeti record her father brought home and a Jacqueline du Pré DVD she found in a shop. After leaving the church as a teenager she started pushing reggae, blues and funk through the cello.

In Mexico City she worked with players including Libertad Figueroa, Gudrun Gut and Julián Bonequi, and met [[Héctor Tosta|1e57c09c-5d04-4df1-916a-1e806e4a2f27]], the future other half of Titanic, along with the musicians who became the collective [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]].

eras.title: Cello records before the band
eras.text: Before Titanic exists, Fratti builds a solo catalogue that moves from chamber quiet to something louder, and The Guardian and Pitchfork start paying attention.

years.h: Pies Sobre La Tierra takes its cue from a W.G. Sebald book
years.p: Fratti's first album draws on Sebald's The Rings of Saturn.

years.h: The Guardian and Pitchfork both cover Será Que Ahora Podremos Entendernos
years.p: The Guardian reviewed Fratti's second album in May 2021 as "soundscaped cello, synths and nature".

years.h: Se Ve Desde Aquí turns Fratti into a European festival act
years.p: That's [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]]'s Daniel Lopatin on her third album, and the record carries her well past Mexico City.
years.xp:
Wikipedia quotes Lopatin's "mind blowing" verdict on Se Ve Desde Aquí, and The Guardian reviewed it in September 2022 as cathartic, powerful experimentation. The Locomotion, a Brussels radio show, later had her on to talk about the record, her Café Oto residency and the Mexican capital's alternative scene.

Lopatin's ear matters later: three years on he plays on Titanic's second album.

eras.title: Titanic sails
eras.text: Tosta, who makes records as I. la Católica, and Fratti stop guesting on each other's projects and become a band with a name. Fratti's solo career and the wider Mexico City circle around them keep running.

years.h: Titanic cut Vidrio in three Mexico City studios
years.p: Eight songs of chamber pop and jazz, made at Tinho, Progreso Nacional and Pedro y el Lobo, released on October 20 by Unheard of Hope.
years.xp: Our Culture's announcement lists the eight tracks: "Anónima", "Circulo Perfecto", "Cielo Falso", "Hotel Elizabeth", "En Paralelo", "Te evite", "Palacio" and "Balanza". Two of them, "Anónima" and "Hotel Elizabeth", came out ahead of the album. Beats Per Minute put it in its top 50 albums of 2023, and The Guardian's review called the pair a joyous Mexico City duo unbounded by genre.

years.h: Titanic record "Hotel Elizabeth" in the Bratislava hotel it's named for
years.p: The same hotel supplies the cover image of Vidrio.
years.xp: José Ostos directed the video, which runs on surreal and unsettling imagery. Fratti told Our Culture that her voice sits "super relaxed" in the song's key and that she was thinking of Chet Baker's smooth delivery.

years.h: Amor Muere, the collective Fratti played in, releases its album
years.p: [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]] (Fratti, Concepción Huerta, Gibrana Cervantes, Camille Mandoki) put out A Time to Love, a Time to Die, the same year as Vidrio.

years.src: Metacritic: Sentir Que No Sabes · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Back on her own, Fratti releases Sentir Que No Sabes
years.p: The Guardian gave it 100. Metacritic lists a Metascore of 86 from 10 reviews, all positive.
years.xp:
Metacritic lists the release date as June 28, 2024 and the label as Revolver USA. The Skinny said she uses "her cello, or some out-of-nowhere sonic texture, to constantly colour outside the lines".

Pitchfork had run a profile that March titled "Chasing the Goblin With Mabe Fratti, the Guatemalan Cellist at the Heart of Mexico City's Avant-Rock Scene", a reference Wikipedia gives.

eras.title: Two producers, one New York studio
eras.text: Titanic take the pop-adjacent debut and blow the doors off: a New York studio, two producers, one guest synth player who wanted in, and a European tour that ran from late August into October.

years.h: "La dueña" starts as warm-up chords backstage at a Ben Howard show
years.p: Tosta found the chord progression in Austria before the show, then dreamed the song into a heartbroken old lady betrayed by love.
years.xp: Tosta told Beats Per Minute the idea grew on the flight back to Mexico, and that karaoke nights at a Mexico City bar pushed him to try a full-hearted ballad. The video borrows telenovela looks.

years.h: A residency in the Netherlands yields "Gotera"
years.p: The lead single, announced with the album by Stereogum, began as material for a commission at a venue in Den Bosch.
years.xp: The band described the song as about "keeping up and moving forward as everything around us is on fire", per Stereogum. Drummer Eli Keszler improvises percussion toward the record's close.

q: Sometimes there's ideas that he would love and I'm like 'no, no, no.'
years.src: Metacritic: Hagen · Album of the Year: HAGEN · Album of the Year: Pitchfork · Paste · BOMB · Treble
yt: Titanic live at the ICA, London
years.p: Metacritic lists the score as 77. Pitchfork later ranked the record No. 19 on its 50 best albums of 2025; The Guardian placed it No. 24.
years.xp:
Metacritic's summary of Pitchfork's review: "The music on HAGEN isn't impenetrable, though it is gargantuan." Other scores it lists: The Guardian 100, Paste 85 (Devon Chodzin) and Mojo 60. Album of the Year also lists Spectrum Culture at 68, and puts the critic average at 78 from five reviews.

BOMB heard black metal, drone, pedal steel, chamber pop and power ballads in the mix. Treble's Jeff Terich, reviewing it, quoted Fratti on the process: "sometimes there's ideas that he would love and I'm like 'no, no, no.'" Treble credits the label as Tin Angel/Unheard of Hope; Metacritic and Album of the Year say Unheard of Hope.

years.h: Daniel Lopatin adds synths to "Pájaro de fuego"
years.p: [[Daniel Lopatin|d5cd6528-3185-4f1b-a297-807b00b16f83]] of Oneohtrix Point Never records the parts during the final stretch of recording.
years.xp: According to FLOOD, HAGEN was recorded at Circular Ruin in New York with producers Nate Salon and [[Randall Dunn|f2be6d74-fac1-4199-9ddc-f3f280630994]]. Dunn tweaked an effects rack on the drums, adding gated reverb that Tosta and Fratti say lifted the groove of "Libra". Salon sampled Keszler's drums for "Gallina degollada".
